// debounce.ts
export function debounce(fn: (...args: any[]) => void, waitMs: number) {
    let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
    return (...args: any[]) => {
        if (timer !== null) {
            return; // already scheduled
        }
        timer = setTimeout(() => fn(args), waitMs);
        timer = null;
    };
}

The intended behavior: debounce(fn, waitMs) returns a function that delays calling fn until
waitMs milliseconds have passed since the LAST call, passing through the latest arguments,
and cancelling any pending call when a new one arrives.

and add a small self-test that runs when the file is executed directly and prints "all tests passed".

// debounce.ts
export function debounce(fn: (...args: any[]) => void, waitMs: number) {
    let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
    return (...args: any[]) => {
        if (timer !== null) {
            return; // already scheduled

        timer = setTimeout(() => fn(args), waitMs);
        timer = null;
    };

The intended behavior: debounce(fn, waitMs) returns a function that delays calling fn until
waitMs milliseconds have passed since the LAST call, passing through the latest arguments,

## Bug Analysis

**What is wrong with the original `debounce.ts`:**

When a new invocation arrives while a previous debounced call is still pending (`timer !== null`), the code simply `return`s early — but it **never cancels the previously scheduled `setTimeout`**. The old timer continues ticking and will eventually call `fn` with the **stale/old arguments**, violating the requirement to "cancel any pending call when a new one arrives."

## Corrected Module

The fix is straightforward: call `clearTimeout(timer)` when a new invocation arrives, before scheduling the new timer.
